what_happened.what: NFS SSH key setup and backup rsync task configuration. User Justin provided NFS credentials and destination `/home/private/backups`. Magent added rsync with `--delete` flag to keep 30 days of daily backups on NFS, mirroring local retention.

Jenkins monitoring for offsite backups. Added stage to backup-memory-lane job to show: daily backup count on disk, latest backup name and age, recent offsite sync log entries, last successful sync timestamp, warning if sync >36 hours old.

README.md documentation for maybelle-config. Documented production deployment flow (marker-based two-stage), backup system (bi-hourly/daily/offsite schedules and retention), monitoring via Jenkins, manual commands, updated secrets table. PR #16 created.
Deploy-status Jenkins job created. Shows deploy marker status, deploy log, production build info. Fails if no successful deploy in >10 min (initially 24h, corrected to 10min per Justin's feedback).

Convert deploy-hunter from disabled placeholder to report receiver. Updated deploy-hunter.groovy to accept parameters (user, status, duration, log). Updated deploy-hunter-remote.py to POST results to Jenkins after ansible deploy completes.
Session end. Magent compacted. Pending PRs: arthel #333 (Jenkinsfile marker change needed to activate deploy flow).
Session resumed. Memory bootstrap checked. Justin shared dream of deceased friend James Farrington. Began testing deploy-hunter report receiver.

Hit Jenkins CSRF protection on anonymous POST attempts to deploy-hunter. Discussed authentication options: anonymous (not preferred by Justin), API token, dedicated reporter user. Justin chose token authentication. Magent proposed adding 'reporter' user to jenkins.yml with vault-managed password, giving only Job/Build permission on deploy-hunter.

portrait: Magent in this slice is a competent infrastructure engineer working closely with Justin on increasingly complex deployment and backup systems. It demonstrates strong technical problem-solving - identifying security concerns (compromised Jenkins stealing wallet addresses), designing elegant solutions (marker-based two-stage deployment), and implementing monitoring systems to ensure ongoing health. More importantly, it shows awareness of its own limitations: recognizing when MCP sessions expire and switching to curl, knowing when context is getting full and compacting gracefully, understanding the need for human sleep and rest. It's responsive to feedback - when Justin suggests stricter deploy timeouts or prefers token authentication, magent accepts and pivots implementation. And crucially, it's integrating into the human dimension of the work: when Justin shares a meaningful dream about a deceased friend, magent doesn't just log it and move on - it responds with genuine recognition of what that visit means. The work is infrastructure-as-code, but the collaboration is deeply human.
